final_message:
**Status: partial.** The function is pinned down and matches the model on every held-out input, but the circuit is not verified: the lab returned `not-verified` on both verification runs. All numbers are from `local-full` (full precision).

**Algorithm**

```python
def predict(tokens, prompt):
    rank = {7: 5, 5: 4, 4: 3, 3: 2, 2: 1, 6: 0}   # pa > bo > pu > ri > ti > so
    return max(tokens[1:], key=lambda t: rank[t])
```

The model outputs the highest-priority symbol present, regardless of position.

**Mechanism, as far as measured**
- **Layer-1 heads 1.0 and 1.1** attend from the last position to the winning symbol (0.83 and 0.92 of their attention, E0008). Mean-ablating both leaves 17% of the logit difference (E0009).
- **mlp1** writes the answer: the layer-1 heads have only about 0.10 direct effect on the logits each (E0012), and ablating mlp1 leaves 29% (E0016).
- **Layer-0 heads 0.0 and 0.1** have almost no direct effect on the logits (E0012). They act mainly through the values the layer-1 heads move (0.18 and 0.23, E0013); ablating both leaves 27% (E0010).
- **mlp0** is also needed: ablating it leaves 23% (E0015).

I found no inert component at head/MLP level, despite the task statement saying some exist. Head 0.0 is the weakest, but it still carries a 0.30 patching effect (E0006).

**Verification**

| Run | Circuit | Agreement with model | Circuit ablated | Circuit alone | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| V0001 (seed 2) | all 6 components | 200/200 | 1% of logit diff, accuracy 0.28 | 100% | not-verified: no sufficiency null is possible when the circuit is the whole model |
| V0002 (seed 3) | all except head 0.0 | 200/200 | −3%, accuracy 0.24 | 68.2%, accuracy 0.965 | not-verified: just under the 0.7 threshold, though it beats all null controls |

I committed in the notebook to that single smaller circuit before running it and did not try further subsets.

**Predictions:** 10 pre-registered, 9 confirmed, 1 refuted (hit rate 0.9). The miss was N0020: I expected layer-0 heads not to feed layer-1 values, and they do.

**Budget:** 16 of 25 experiments used (5 exploratory), plus the 2 verification runs.

**Gaps**
- The path-patching primitive rejected `mlp0` as a sender, so the edges into and out of the MLPs are inferred from ablations, not measured as paths.
- How the layer-1 heads identify the winner, and what exactly layer 0 adds to the values, is unresolved.
- An all-`so` input never appeared in the samples, so the rule's prediction of `so` there is untested.
